articles.title: Bristol Bake Off star says 'going sober' has been 'glorious'
articles.summary: Briony May Williams has been sober since 2023 after deciding to make "big changes" in her life.
articles.body:
A Great British Bake Off star turned TV presenter says "going sober" and being alcohol free for nearly three years has been "glorious".

Briony May Williams, from Bristol, made it to the Great British Bake Off semi-finals back in 2018, but went home after she served judges Paul Hollywood and Prue Leith "raw pastry" and admitted she used "salt instead of sugar".

Williams said she decided to make some "big changes" in her life and go sober after she ended up in hospital at the end of 2023 following an "alcohol-heavy 39th birthday".

"Going sober - it's glorious. It's not always easy but it's always worth it and I feel much more able to cope with what life throws at me," she added.

Nipple tattooist 'frustrated' by online censorship

'You never quite know what you're going to pull out'

Since her first TV appearance on the popular cooking show, Williams has built a career as a presenter, working for BBC One shows Morning Live and Escape To The Country, as well as Channel 4's Food Unwrapped.

But Williams said hitting the 1000 days alcohol-free milestone at the end of July felt like "such a massive achievement".

"It felt really huge. Getting through another summer and not wanting alcohol.

It's been a huge mind shift but now its just a normal part of my life," she added.

She said she was never addicted to alcohol, but as a social drinker she did love "a vino or five on a night out".

But when she realised alcohol "wasn't bringing anything positive" to her life she decided to take it "one day at a time" without thinking about how far she would get.

"When you're feeling vulnerable you can turn to booze and I feel a bit of dread in the run-up to Christmas and the New Year," she said.

"But the thought of going back to it fills me with dread.

"Now, I have a cup of tea and give my daughter a cuddle. I'm OK without it now - I don't think I'll ever go back."

Despite being eight years "out of the Bake Off tent" and "part of the vintage crop of bakers", Williams said she is still a massive fan of the show.

"I do have a Bake Off tattoo on my ribs - I've got a piping bag, a whisk and a rolling pin," she said.

"It's quite funny - during the series we were all like let's get a tattoo - as far as I'm aware I'm the only one who got a tattoo.

"But you know it was such an amazing part of my life, it's completely changed my life in so many wonderful ways."

The 17th series of the Channel 4 show will return on 22 September and will see TV chef Nigella Lawson taking over from Dame Prue Leith in the Bake Off tent alongside Paul Hollywood.

Contestants have also been confirmed , including a paediatric doctor, a competitive sprinter, a hairdresser and a drag artist.

Briony said she is "really excited" to see Nigella and Paul "in the tent together".

"I mean Prue used to give it to you honestly. She would tell you if your cake was rubbish, you know, like when your Nan says something really mean but she doesn't mean it to be mean," she said.

"But I'd be really intimidated baking for [Nigella]."

articles.title: Único veterano vivo da 2ª Guerra no ES ganha medalha aos 103 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Agostinho Ferreira da Silva recebeu a condecoração 'Soldado da Paz', entregue pelos Boinas-Azuis da Organização das Nações Unidas, e ganhou nova versão da medalha 'Sangue do Brasil'. No Brasil, ainda existem 19 combatentes sobreviventes vivos, segundo a FEB.
articles.summary: Agostinho Ferreira da Silva recebeu a condecoração 'Soldado da Paz', entregue pelos Boinas-Azuis da Organização das Nações Unidas, e ganhou nova versão da medalha 'Sangue do Brasil
articles.body:
O último veterano da Segunda Guerra Mundial que mora no Espírito Santo recebeu uma medalha da Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU) na última quarta-feira (23). Agostinho Ferreira da Silva, de 103 anos, é ex-combatente da Força Expedicionária Brasileira (FEB), enviada à Itália em 1945.

A solenidade aconteceu no Tiro de Guerra de Guaçuí , no Sul do estado, onde o ex-militar mora. Ele recebeu a condecoração 'Soldado da Paz', concedida pelo presidente e integrantes da Associação capixaba dos Boinas-Azuis, grupo que atua nas Forças de Manutenção da Paz da ONU .

Um vídeo (assista acima) registrou o momento em que Agostinho se emociona ao ser homenageado entre familiares e outros militares. Ao ouvir que "suas lágrimas são de honra, heroísmo, honestidade e patriotismo", o veterano acrescentou outra grande questão que o emocionou: a amizade.

"Muito obrigado pela homenagem. A presença de todos vocês deixou meu coração assim, aberto para todo mundo", agradeceu Agostinho. Segundo a família, ele ficou muito feliz e emocionado também pela pela quantidade de militares de outras regiões que apareceram para vê-lo.

No Brasil, segundo dados do Censo Permamente da FEB, apenas 19 combatentes sobreviventes da Segunda Guerra Mundial foram identificados ainda vivos no país em setembro de 2026.

Agostinho Ferreira da Silva, último veterano da Segunda Guerra Mundial no ES, ganhou medalha da ONU aos 103 anos — Foto: Divulgação/Tiro de Guerra de Guaçuí

Segundo o neto, o advogado Felipe Campos, o avô tem alzheimer, mas em todas as homenagens que ele recebe e o Exército está presente, ele lembra e se emociona.

"O vô sempre foi uma pessoa muito simples e sempre incentivos eu e minha irmã a seguir o caminho dos estudos. Foi muito importante na nossa vida, sempre tivemos ele como um exemplo de caráter", contou.

O veterano também ganhou uma nova versão da Medalha de Guerra 'Sangue do Brasil', recebida ao final da guerra por sua participação e honra.

“Estamos repondo essa medalha, que é a original do senhor e está 'velhinha' pelo tempo. Essa aqui está mais conservada e o senhor vai continuar tendo a honra de levá-la no peito, simbolizando todo o seu sacrifício nos campos de batalha da Itália", disse o militar que aparece no vídeo colocando a nova insígnia no veterano.

De acordo com o site oficial do Museu Virtual da Força Expedicionária Brasileira, a medalha 'Sangue do Brasil' foi criada pelo Decreto-Lei nº 7.709, de 5 de julho de 1945, com o objetivo de homenagear militares brasileiros feridos por inimigos durante as operações na Itália.

Agostinho recebeu a insígnia pela primeira vez após ser atingido por estilhaços de granada em 17 de abril de 1945, quando atuava na região italiana de Castel d'Aiano. Na época, o soldado tinha apenas 22 anos de idade.

articles.title: Livros obrigatórios Unicamp: como revisar na reta final do vestibular | G1
articles.standfirst: Professora orienta a priorizar enredo, personagens, temas e contexto histórico, além de indicar alternativas para quem não conseguiu fazer a leitura completa.
articles.summary: Professora orienta a priorizar enredo, personagens, temas e contexto histórico, além de indicar alternativas para quem não conseguiu fazer a leitura completa.
articles.body:
A Unicamp cobra nove obras literárias obrigatórias no vestibular , nas provas da primeira e da segunda fase. Na reta final, porém, como revisar tantos livros sem precisar reler tudo? E quem não conseguiu fazer as leituras, ainda pode recuperar parte do conteúdo?

A educadora popular Jennifer Patrocínio, que dá aulas de redação, linguagens, gramática e literatura no Cursinho Popular Herbert de Souza, recomenda priorizar os principais elementos de cada obra , como, por exemplo:

Além disso, segundo ela, fichamentos e releituras de trechos importantes podem facilitar a revisão. Para quem ainda tem tempo de voltar aos livros, a orientação é fazer uma leitura atenta e retomar os pontos mais importantes.

Já quem não conseguiu ler as obras pode recorrer a análises e resumos para conhecer os principais temas e contextos, embora esse estudo seja mais superficial – veja abaixo a lista de livros indicados e mais dicas de como estudar.

"O que atravessa essa obra historicamente, socialmente, o que está por trás, relembrar um pouco também da história, é importante, ir atrás de outras interpretações, de percepções críticas, de como essa obra é cobrada nos vestibulares também", comenta.

📚 Esta reportagem compõe o projeto Vestibulou , uma iniciativa do g1 Campinas para divulgar informações relacionadas aos principais vestibulares e ajudar na preparação dos estudantes.

Confira a lista de obras obrigatórias, que deve ser lida ao longo do ano por quem está se preparando. Entre os títulos estão:

“Canções escolhidas”, de Paulo César Pinheiro

“Memórias Póstumas de Brás Cubas”, de Machado de Assis

“Morangos mofados” (contos escolhidos), de Caio Fernando Abreu

“No seu pescoço”, de Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie

“Os funerais da Mamãe Grande”, de Gabriel García Márquez

“Prosas seguidas de odes mínimas”, de José Paulo Paes

“Vida e morte de M. J. Gonzaga de Sá”, de Lima Barreto

Biblioteca no Cursinho Popular Herbert de Souza — Foto: Isabelly Godoy

Além dos fichamentos, Jennifer recomenda conteúdos online, como vídeos de análise literária produzidos por especialistas e criadores de conteúdo. Segundo ela, esse material ajuda os estudantes a revisar os principais pontos das obras.

A professora diz que os vídeos ajudam a reforçar a compreensão das obras e a relembrar detalhes importantes para a prova.

Jennifer também orienta os candidatos a relacionar as obras aos contextos histórico e social. Segundo ela, a Unicamp costuma cobrar questões que conectam a literatura a temas mais amplos da sociedade.

"Assim, das recomendações que a gente traz e pensando no que eles trazem também em sala de aula, acho que esses links e essas relações vão muito das associações que eles vão fazendo. Então, ok, é uma obra de 1850, por exemplo. O que a gente tem dentro desse contexto histórico?", diz.

Jennifer também recomenda a releitura de trechos importantes, especialmente os que ajudam a compreender personagens centrais ou temas relevantes da obra.

Segundo ela, revisitar partes do livro ajuda a manter as informações na memória. A professora afirma que os estudantes não devem depender apenas das anotações, mas também voltar à obra para construir novas interpretações.

Para a educadora, embora a situação seja mais difícil, quem não conseguiu ler as obras ainda pode recorrer a vídeos de análise e resumos disponíveis na internet.

Segundo ela, esse material pode servir como um primeiro contato com a obra para quem não conseguiu fazer a leitura completa. Ainda assim, a recomendação é ler os livros sempre que possível, mesmo que parcialmente.

Jennifer avalia que ainda é possível aproveitar o tempo restante para ler algumas obras ou, ao menos, compreender seus principais temas e contextos por meio de análises e resumos.

Para ela, embora esse tipo de preparação seja mais superficial, os resumos podem ajudar o candidato a compreender as principais características da obra, o contexto histórico e os temas abordados.

⚠️ Possíveis riscos para os não-leitores

A professora alerta que quem não leu as obras pode enfrentar dificuldades. Segundo ela, provas de anos anteriores mostram que a Unicamp costuma cobrar detalhes específicos dos livros.

Para minimizar esse risco, Jennifer orienta os estudantes a recuperar o máximo possível de informações sobre as obras e usar os conhecimentos adquiridos em análises e resumos para fazer inferências durante a prova.

Jennifer recomenda cautela com adaptações para cinema e televisão. Segundo ela, essas produções são interpretações das obras originais e nem sempre reproduzem fielmente seu conteúdo.

Ela cita como exemplo adaptações que apresentam novas interpretações dos personagens e do contexto retratado no livro. No geral, essas produções podem ser interessantes, mas não substituem o contato com a obra original.

*Estagiária sob supervisão de Yasmin Castro.

articles.title: São Cosme e Damião: a origem da tradição de distribuir doces | G1
articles.standfirst: Tradição é celebrada no Vale do Paraíba e região e reúne costumes do catolicismo e das religiões de matriz africana.
articles.summary: A celebração de São Cosme e Damião une catolicismo e religiões de matriz africana em uma tradição de fé e distribuição de doces no Vale do Paraíba.
articles.body:
Festa de São Cosme e Damião na Tenda de Umbanda Senzala dos Pretos Velhos, em São José dos Campos (SP) — Foto: Vinicius Aires

A história e devoção a São Cosme e Damião atravessam diferentes religiões e são lembradas pelo costume de distribuir doces às crianças . Essa tradição, celebrada no Vale do Paraíba e região, assim como em todo o Brasil, foi resultado de uma mistura da Igreja Católica com as religiões de matriz africana.

🗓️ A diferença na data também acompanha as tradições de cada vertente. No catolicismo, os santos são lembrados em 26 de setembro. Já nas religiões afro-brasileiras, a data associada aos dois é 27 de setembro.

Segundo o presbítero da Diocese de São José dos Campos (SP), Padre Edinei Batista, Cosme e Damião eram irmãos gêmeos e médicos que viveram por volta do século IV, e dedicaram suas vidas aos cuidados com os mais necessitados e a Deus.

"Eles eram cristãos, de origem oriental, e eram médicos. Atendiam as pessoas e faziam o bem, cuidavam de quem precisava de maneira gratuita, não recebendo por isso, sobretudo dos pobres. E, por serem seguidores de Cristo, também faziam isso, gastando a sua vida, seu conhecimento a serviço de quem mais precisava", contou o padre.

Durante o Império de Diocleciano, em Roma, os santos foram perseguidos e mortos.

Por serem mártires, foram canonizados ainda na antiguidade. Eles também são considerados padroeiros de profissionais da área da saúde , como médicos, enfermeiros e farmacêuticos.

Apesar de pessoas de diferentes crenças distribuírem doces às crianças, o padre explica que a prática não faz parte da celebração na Igreja Católica.

Segundo a dirigente espiritual da Tenda de Umbanda Senzala dos Pretos Velhos, em São José dos Campos, Katia Moreira, a ação começou a partir de uma mistura das religiões de matriz africana com o catolicismo.

De acordo com Katia, devido à perseguição e preconceito, a Umbanda associou São Cosme e Damião aos orixás Ibejis, que também são gêmeos, e às entidades Erês, que representam a infância.

"Quando o povo negro vem para o Brasil, cada um cultuava os seus orixás, cultuava os seus inquices, os seus voduns. E em terras brasileiras, eles não tinham permissão, havia preconceito, tudo que vinha do negro era ruim, era demoníaco. Então, pra poderem cultuar as suas divindades, eles sincretizavam em santos que mais se assemelhavam", explicou a dirigente espiritual.

Por cultuarem orixás e entidades relacionadas às crianças e associarem com a imagem de São Cosme e Damião, a distribuição de doces se tornou parte da celebração.

Além disso, segundo Katia, a festa também reúne pessoas de outras religiões e é aberta ao público.

"Eu sei que ainda existe uma luta com relação a aceitar, achar que isso é coisa do demônio. Mas a gente procura trazer esse pessoal pra perto da gente, pra entenderem que o nosso trabalho não é esse, muito pelo contrário. Nosso trabalho é trazer esperança. Quem é que consegue ficar triste comendo bolo de chocolate?", comentou Katia.

Para ela, compartilhar os alimentos é uma forma de mostrar o significado da tradição e aproximar pessoas de diferentes crenças.

Já na Igreja Católica, a data é celebrada com missas e orações em homenagem aos santos. A distribuição de doces não é considerada um pecado no catolicismo , porém não faz parte da religião, segundo o padre.

De acordo com ele, o foco da celebração na Igreja está no exemplo de fé, no amor ao próximo e no serviço aos necessitados.

articles.title: Justiça reconhece pai biológico e mantém pai socioafetivo no registro de criança em SC; entenda | G1
articles.standfirst: Divulgada pela 2ª Vara da Família de Joinville, decisão judicial considerou que o vínculo afetivo construído entre eles deve ser preservado.
articles.summary: Divulgada pela 2ª Vara da Família de Joinville, decisão judicial considerou que o vínculo afetivo construído entre eles deve ser preservado.
articles.body:
Prédio do Tribunal de Justiça de Santa Catarina — Foto: Mauricio Vieira/NCI TJSC/Divulgação

A Justiça de Santa Catarina reconheceu a paternidade biológica de um homem e, ao mesmo tempo, manteve no registro civil a paternidade socioafetiva de outro homem , que assumiu a função de pai desde o nascimento da criança ( entenda mais abaixo ).

A decisão, divulgada na quinta-feira (23) pela 2ª Vara da Família de Joinville , no Norte, considerou que o vínculo afetivo construído entre o pai socioafetivo e a criança deverá ser preservado .

De acordo com o processo, a criança foi registrada ao nascer pela mãe e pelo então companheiro dela, que sabia que poderia não ser o pai biológico. Anos depois, um exame de DNA confirmou a paternidade de outro homem. Com o resultado, a família pediu à Justiça a inclusão do pai biológico e a exclusão do pai registral .

Durante a ação, o Ministério Público (MP) concordou com o reconhecimento da paternidade biológica, mas solicitou um estudo social antes de avaliar a retirada do vínculo socioafetivo . O laudo psicológico apontou que o pai registral exerceu a função paterna de forma ativa nos primeiros anos da criança.

Na avaliação, a criança reconheceu ambos como pais . Um estudo social, por sua vez, apontou que a convivência atual entre ela e o pai socioafetivo havia diminuído, razão pela qual recomendou a retirada da paternidade do registro.

Ao analisar as provas, a Justiça entendeu que o distanciamento recente não apaga o vínculo afetivo construído com a criança. No entendimento da Justiça, o pai socioafetivo teria exercido o seu papel, integrando a família por um período significativo. Com isso, a reorganização familiar posterior não elimina a relação .

Além disso, a sentença destacou que o reconhecimento do pai biológico não impede a manutenção do pai socioafetivo, garantindo a preservação da história de vida da criança.

articles.title: Colombia extradites warlord to U.S. as its security strategy aligns with Washington
articles.summary: A Colombian warlord, whose extradition to the United States had been delayed for several months while he was designated a peace negotiator by the country’s previous government, was flown to California and placed in custody of federal agents.
articles.body: BOGOTA, Colombia — A Colombian warlord, whose extradition to the United States had been delayed for several months while he was designated a peace negotiator by the country’s previous government, was flown to California and placed in custody of federal agents. Geovany Andres Rojas faces drug trafficking and terrorism charges in the United States. For years, he acted as a spokesman and leader of Comandos de la Frontera, a rebel group known for trafficking cocaine in Putumayo, a Colombian province that borders Ecuador and Peru. Rojas, who is also known as “the spider,” had been protected from extradition by former Colombian President Gustavo Petro, who had asked him to participate in peace talks with the Colombian government. But a new government, led by conservative President Abelardo de la Espriella, lifted the ban on Rojas’s extradition, signaling a shift in the nation’s security strategy. “You don’t build peace by protecting narco-terrorists like this bandit,” de la Espriella said Friday, after he personally supervised Rojas’ transfer to the U.S. “I ask U.S. authorities … that he cannot negotiate deals that will leave his crimes unpunished.” Rojas was arrested in Bogota in February 2025, and Colombia’s Supreme Court approved his extradition to the U.S. in October. But Petro suspended it, arguing he needed Rojas to participate in peace talks between the Colombian government and several rebel groups, including Comandos de la Frontera. De la Espriella, who was elected in June, has suspended talks with rebel groups and has taken an iron-fist approach to crime. It recently included militarizing a city in the north of Colombia, where a drug gang attempted to impose a three-day curfew. The conservative leader was endorsed by President Donald Trump while campaigning and has said he will work closely with the United States to fight drug trafficking. Colombia’s government has struggled to contain violence in rural areas in recent years, as drug gangs and rebel groups fight over territory abandoned by the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia or FARC, following their 2016 peace deal with the government. More than 14,000 fighters laid down their weapons as a result of the agreement that ended five decades of guerrilla warfare. But the peace deal also left a power vacuum in regions with little state presence, where illegal activities like the cocaine trade are common. Several breakaway groups are now fighting over drug trafficking routes, illegal mines and extortion rackets in these areas. Comandos de la Frontera emerged in 2017 and is partly led by former FARC fighters who did not join the 2016 peace deal. The group formed an alliance with the Segunda Marquetalia organization, a group founded in 2019 by former FARC commander Luciano Marin. But the alliance fell apart two years ago, leaving Comandos de la Frontera to conduct separate negotiations with Colombia’s government.

articles.title: Body of 10th woman found in South Africa as probe into killings continues
articles.summary: Another woman’s body was found near Johannesburg, bringing to 10 the number of victims in a series of killings under investigation, South African police said Saturday.
articles.body: JOHANNESBURG — Another woman’s body was found near Johannesburg, bringing to 10 the number of victims in a series of killings under investigation, South African police said Saturday. Police began investigating after the bodies of three women were found in July and August within about 4.3 miles of one another in the Ekurhuleni municipality, east of Johannesburg. The discovery of six bodies in Ekurhuleni over 10 days earlier this month raised fears that a serial killer or killers were responsible. Two women were arrested and charged last week with murder in relation to the ninth body, discovered on Sept. 17. The victim had been stabbed and had her throat cut, police said. Police did not link the two women charged to any of the other killings. Provincial police commissioner Lt. Gen. Tommy Mthombeni told state broadcaster SABC on Saturday that investigators believed the ninth killing was an isolated case but could not rule out the possibility that some of the other cases were linked. Police have identified similarities in some of the killings but said they had not found conclusive evidence that the same person or people were responsible. All nine of the bodies discovered before Saturday were those of women in their 20s or 30s, according to police. Several were naked or partially clothed and left in open areas near main roads. Officers from the Investigative Psychology Unit, which specializes in complex or serial violent crimes, are part of the investigation. Police released limited details about the 10th body, which was found early Saturday, and did not immediately identify the victim. “We can only confirm the discovery of the body,” the South African Police Service said in a statement. “Crime scene management and all the necessary role players are currently on the scene.” South Africa has high rates of violent crime and violence against women. The killings in Ekurhuleni have sparked a national outcry over women’s safety.

articles.title: EU unlocks humanitarian aid for crises worldwide
articles.summary: EU allocates majority of aid to sub-Saharan Africa to fund actions related to migration, conflict and food insecurity.
articles.body:
The European Union has pledged to release more than 710 million euros ($810m) to help people affected by crises, natural disasters or conflicts worldwide, particularly in Africa.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen made the announcement in a post on her X account on Saturday, following the cancellation of New York’s Global Citizen Festival, where she was due to speak.

“Conflicts, extreme weather events and rising living costs are throwing the lives of many people around the world into disarray,” she said in a video.

The aid “will support displaced communities across Africa, as well as the communities that host them”, von der Leyen said.

According to a European Commission press release on Saturday, the package allocates 380 million euros ($430m) to fund measures related to migration in sub-Saharan Africa, “focused on the protection of vulnerable migrants, support for voluntary return and reintegration”.

A total of 97 million euros ($110m) is earmarked for sub-Saharan Africa to respond to worsening humanitarian needs caused by conflict, food insecurity, malnutrition and climate shocks across several regions.

The funding “will also reinforce the response to the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and neighbouring countries”, the press statement said.

A further 7.5 million euros ($8.5m) will be deployed to the Democratic Republic of the Congo to support the response to the Ebola crisis and for future preparedness, and 10 million euros ($11.5m) to “support ongoing efforts to promote peace and stability in the Great Lakes region “, which is wracked by armed conflict, humanitarian crises and environmental changes.

The Palestinian territories and Lebanon will receive 103 million euros ($117m) to support vulnerable populations, while Ukraine will get 52 million euros ($59m) for humanitarian assistance and emergency preparedness.

The European Commission also announced three new Global Gateway investments at the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York last week.

The package included an EU guarantee designed to mobilise private investment in health and nutrition businesses in sub-Saharan Africa, an EU-backed European Investment Bank loan to expand vaccine and biological medicines production in Colombia, and 60 million euros ($68m) to strengthen primary healthcare in Ethiopia.

The European Commission said it had allocated 2.5 million euros ($3m) for humanitarian aid since the start of the year.

images.caption: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen arrives ahead of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly at the UN headquarters in New York on September 22, 2026 [Stefan Jeremiah/AP]

articles.title: Archaeologists uncover 2,700-year-old Etruscan tomb at Italy’s Vulci; weapons, gold and rare pottery found in elite burial
articles.summary: Archaeologists have uncovered a monumental Etruscan tomb inside an ancient cemetery at Vulci in central Italy, nearly 140 years after French archaeologist
articles.body: Archaeologists have uncovered a monumental Etruscan tomb inside an ancient cemetery at Vulci in central Italy, nearly 140 years after French archaeologist Stéphane Gsell first identified the burial mound surrounding it. The newly excavated Tomb of the Stone Chamber dates to the late seventh century BCE, one of the most prosperous periods in Vulci's history, when the city also had intense connections with the Mediterranean. The burial contained weapons, chariot fittings, gold and bronze objects, bone and ivory artefacts, high-quality ceramics and an exceptional banquet service. Archaeologist Christian Mazet described it to Etruscan Times as a tomb “of the very highest rank”, based on the nature of its surviving grave goods.A monumental Etruscan tomb hidden inside the Gsell tumulusThe discovery was made during the 2026 excavation campaign in the Polledrara necropolis at ancient Vulci. According to Etruscan Times, the Return to Vulci team identified the great Gsell Tumulus on the ground and brought to light what is in all probability the princely burial that Gsell had searched for but never managed to find. The newly uncovered structure, known as the Tomb of the Stone Chamber, lies within the monumental complex. The 2026 investigation also revealed that the tumulus may be considerably larger than previously believed, although its full dimensions still need to be established through further work.Why archaeologists call it a tomb of the highest rankThe burial's architecture and surviving grave goods point to its exceptional status within Vulci's society. Christian Mazet, one of the scientific directors of the Return to Vulci project, said the presence of weapons, a chariot, gold objects and high-quality ceramics of the type found in princely tombs of the Osteria necropolis showed that the burial belonged to the highest rank. The official Italian Superintendency likewise described the discovery as particularly important for understanding the aristocracy of Vulci at the end of the seventh century BCE. The tomb consists of three chambers, with the walls of the main chamber built from large blocks of nenfro set into natural deposits associated with the ancient course of the Fiora River.Weapons, chariot fittings and an exceptional banquet serviceDespite clandestine intrusions into the tomb during the 20th century, archaeologists found groups of objects in the side chambers that had survived in their original positions. The excavations recovered weapons, chariot fittings, gold and bronze sheets, as well as objects made of bone and ivory. Researchers also found Corinthian pottery and bucchero wares, along with a bronze tripod associated with a lamp made of alabaster gypsum, probably of Aegean origin.The side chambers also contained an important banquet service made from Polledrara Ware, a rare local polychrome pottery that was used by Vulci's leading families. The assemblage included dinoi for mixing wine and water, cups and other vessels for holding liquids, as well as a grater associated with wine preparation. A large polychrome ceremonial cup in the Ionian Wild Goat Style was also recovered, with very close parallels among the grave goods from the Tomb of Isis.Stéphane Gsell identified the mound in 1889The newly uncovered tomb is closely connected to the work of French archaeologist Stéphane Gsell, who investigated the necropolises of Vulci in the late 19th century. In 1889, Gsell identified the large tumulus at Polledrara, reconstructed its perimeter and searched for its main tomb. He eventually had to stop excavating because he no longer had the money or time needed to find the burial. More than a century later, the Return to Vulci team returned to the site and uncovered what it believes is the princely burial Gsell had searched for.What the discovery reveals about ancient VulciThe newly uncovered burial dates to the end of the seventh century BCE, a period when Vulci was experiencing one of the most prosperous phases in its history and maintaining intense connections with the Mediterranean. The wealth and variety of objects recovered from the tomb provide evidence of the high status of the people buried there. The discovery also offers an opportunity to compare the complex with other important Vulci burials, particularly the nearby Tomb of Isis, which was discovered in 1839 and is now associated with the British Museum. According to the Italian Superintendency, similarities between the two complexes could help researchers investigate funerary rituals, artistic production and exchange networks among Vulci's elites at the end of the seventh century BCE.You use AI every day. articles.title: Venezuela frees 39 political prisoners after post-Maduro talks
articles.summary: The releases follow a second round of negotiations between Venezuela’s interim government and the opposition.
articles.body:
More than three dozen political prisoners have been released in Venezuela following a second round of talks backed by Washington between the country’s interim government and the opposition.

Human rights group Justicia, Encuentro y Perdon (JEP) said 39 political dissidents were freed between Friday and Saturday from various prisons, including eight women accused of “narco-terrorism” in 2021 and six people accused of working with the United States in a 2020 attempt to overthrow former President Nicolas Maduro.

“We will remain vigilant and continue to demand full freedom for all those who are still waiting,” JEP said in a statement on X.

The releases followed a second round of negotiations on Friday between the government of interim President Delcy Rodriguez, who was Maduro’s former vice president, and the opposition, held with US approval since Washington’s military removal of Maduro in January.

A first round of talks in August focused on retrieving Venezuelan funds frozen overseas to help recovery from June’s earthquakes, which killed more than 6,300 people, and on reforming the judiciary.

Rodriguez enacted an amnesty law in February under US pressure, though the pace of releases has been slow.

Foro Penal, a rights group that tracks political detentions, said 344 people remained classified as political prisoners as of September 18, down from 391 on August 10, when the government said it had freed 131 people under a separate “alternative measures” programme.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said at the time that more than 1,000 Venezuelans had been released since Maduro’s removal, calling it “a crucial step” for the country’s reconciliation.

Families of political prisoners have staged ongoing protests outside the US embassy in Caracas and the El Rodeo I prison, which rights groups consider a torture centre.

articles.title: Israeli UN envoy's Starlink video reaches millions, with nearly 40% of Instagram viewers in Iran
articles.summary: Danny Danon's viral Starlink video drew 9 million views, with nearly 40% of Instagram viewers in Iran, his office says, prompting a counter-campaign.
articles.body: A viral video of Israel’s U.N. ambassador offering an Iranian representative a Starlink device has reached around 9 million views across social media — and nearly 40% of its Instagram viewers are in Iran, according to analytics shared with Fox News Digital. A representative for Israeli Ambassador to the U.N. Danny Danon told Fox News Digital that the office was surprised by the video’s reach inside Iran, saying such an audience is unusual for Israeli diplomatic accounts. "We couldn't imagine to be the popular," the representative said, referring to the video's reach in Iran. MIDDLE EAST TAKES CENTER STAGE AT UN AS REGIONAL LEADERS CONFRONT IRAN WAR, GAZA AND HOUTHI THREAT The representative said the encounter grew out of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s address to the U.N. General Assembly, where Netanyahu displayed a Starlink device while delivering a message aimed at the Iranian people. According to Danon’s representative, Netanyahu had prepared the Starlink element for his speech and asked that the device be offered to the Iranian delegation afterward. Danon then approached an Iranian representative with the device in an encounter captured on video. The Iranian representative declined to take it. TRUMP, IRANIAN PRESIDENT CONVERGE ON NYC FOR ‘DRAMATIC’ UN SHOWDOWN AS TEHRAN FACES TIGHT RESTRICTIONS Danon later posted the exchange on social media, where the video quickly gained traction. Instagram audience analytics shared with Fox News Digital show 39.9% of viewers were located in Iran, the largest share from any country. The U.S. accounted for 14.3%, followed by Israel at 12.6%, Canada at 5.9% and Germany at 4.1%. The representative said Danon’s office viewed the unusually large Iranian audience as significant given the message accompanying the Starlink offer, which he described as one of freedom and freedom of expression for the Iranian people. IRAN ACCELERATES EXECUTION CAMPAIGN AGAINST ANTI-REGIME ACTIVISTS AMID INTERNET CENSORSHIP But Danon’s office says another online trend emerged as the video spread. The representative told Fox News Digital that accounts the office believes are Iranian began recirculating a years-old video of former Israeli Ambassador to the U.N. Gilad Erdan being escorted from the General Assembly during a protest against then-Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi. The video dates to September 2023, when Erdan walked through the General Assembly holding a photograph of Mahsa Amini during Raisi’s speech. One post recirculating the old video in recent hours has drawn hundreds of thousands of views while portraying the incident as a current confrontation involving Israel’s U.N. ambassador. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Danon’s representative characterized the renewed circulation as a "disinformation campaign" intended to counter the attention surrounding Danon’s video. "From our perspective, the Danon video moved something in Iran," the representative told Fox News Digital, arguing that the Iranian regime was attempting to "change the story." Fox News Digital's Emma Bussey contributed to this report.

articles.title: Nepalese security guard won UAE’s Dh30 million lottery jackpot; he plans to split the $8.2 million fortune with 4 friends
articles.summary: Tayab Khan, a 26-year-old Nepalese security guard working in Abu Dhabi's Ruwais Industrial Area, became the first winner of the UAE Lottery's new Dh30
articles.body: Tayab Khan, a 26-year-old Nepalese security guard working in Abu Dhabi's Ruwais Industrial Area, became the first winner of the UAE Lottery's new Dh30 million grand prize after matching all 7 winning numbers in a May 27, 2026 draw. Khan did not watch the draw and instead discovered the result through an email notification during the Eid Al Adha holiday. The Dh30 million jackpot, worth roughly $8.2 million, was not his alone. Khan had bought the ticket as part of a 5-member syndicate called Future Millionaires, meaning the prize will be divided equally among him and 4 friends, giving each member Dh6 million, or about $1.64 million. Khan has said he plans to leave his security job, build a home for his family in Nepal and learn more about investment and business opportunities, while allowing himself a few luxuries, including a Mahindra Thar and a Rolex watch. This remarkable win demonstrates how persistent collective effort among close friends can transform ordinary aspirations into extraordinary opportunities, ultimately strengthening both personal relationships and financial futures.The syndicate had been playing together for 18 monthsKhan moved from Nepal's Gorkha district to the UAE about 4 years ago and has worked as a security guard in the Ruwais Industrial Area. He had been participating in the UAE Lottery regularly since its launch, which took place in December 2024, and continued playing with his friends despite not initially winning a major prize. The group pooled money to buy lottery tickets and called themselves Future Millionaires, a name Khan chose before their eventual win. After the jackpot, he said he changed the group's name to simply "Millionaires". Two of his fellow syndicate members, Sandeep BK and Shishir Paudel, joined Khan when he spoke about the win at the UAE Lottery's offices. The winning draw was held on Wednesday, May 27. Khan had selected all 7 winning numbers at random and was not watching the live broadcast when the results were announced. Instead, he received an email later that evening. He initially expected the message to relate to one of the smaller prizes he had won in previous draws. When he opened it and saw Dh30 million, he said his hands and legs began shaking and that he could not speak.Each of the 5 friends will receive Dh6 millionThe friends had regularly pooled their money to participate, with the winning ticket bought collectively. The Dh30 million jackpot will therefore be divided equally between all 5 members of the syndicate. That leaves each person with Dh6 million, equivalent to roughly $1.64 million. Khan described the money as an opportunity to provide greater financial security for his family and said the win could give his friends the freedom to take new opportunities in their own lives. The group had already experienced smaller lottery wins, which encouraged them to continue participating. Khan said there had been periods when it felt as though the jackpot might never come, but the friends continued to believe they could eventually win.Khan plans to build a home for his family in NepalKhan's first major priority is building a house for his family in Nepal. He has said that owning a good home for his parents and wider family was already one of his biggest goals, and the jackpot will allow him to build the kind of house he had previously hoped for. He also intends to leave his job as a security guard and explore entrepreneurship and investment. After working as an employee for 4 years, Khan said he now wants to learn more about investing and move towards a different stage of his working life. His plans extend beyond the immediate financial windfall. Khan has spoken about using the money to create greater security for his family, while also taking time to consider what he wants to do next rather than making every decision immediately after the win.A Mahindra Thar and Rolex are among his personal plansWhile most of Khan's stated priorities involve his family and his future, he has also identified a couple of personal purchases he has wanted for years. He told Gulf News and Khaleej Times that a Mahindra Thar SUV and a Rolex watch are both on his wish list. The purchases sit alongside his plans to build a family home and explore investment and business opportunities. Khan has also said he has not yet settled on all of his long-term plans. For now, the immediate focus is on celebrating the win with the four friends who shared the ticket and on working out how to use the money responsibly.The win came after the UAE Lottery changed its jackpot formatKhan's jackpot came shortly after the UAE Lottery changed its grand-prize structure. The lottery launched in December 2024 with a Dh100 million grand prize, but changed to a format offering a Dh30 million top prize on a twice-weekly schedule in April 2026. Khan's May 27 win was the first Dh30 million grand-prize victory under the new format. The Lucky Day draw uses a calendar-style format. Players select 6 numbers from 1 to 31 in the "day" section and 1 number from 1 to 12 in the "month" section, making 7 selections in total. Khan matched all 7 numbers in the May 27 draw. Participants must be UAE residents aged at least 18 and register through the lottery's official platform.Khan has also urged other players to approach the lottery responsibly. His message after the win was not simply to keep buying tickets, but to participate within limits and only spend money that would not interfere with everyday expenses. For Khan and his 4 friends, the Dh30 million jackpot has transformed a routine lottery syndicate into a shared fortune. Each of the 5 members now has Dh6 million, while Khan plans to use his share first to provide his family with a home before exploring the investment opportunities that could shape his next chapter.You use AI every day. articles.title: Boeing identifies 737 MAX software glitch affecting landing navigation feature
articles.summary: Boeing has identified a previously undisclosed 737 MAX software glitch that could cause an automated navigation feature to fail during landing, The Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday, citing company documents.
articles.body: Boeing has identified a previously undisclosed 737 MAX software glitch that could cause an automated navigation feature to fail during landing, The Wall Street Journal reported on Saturday, citing company documents. The issue emerged from a cockpit software update and can occur when flight crews alter their planned flight path after a missed approach, the report said. When reached for comment, Boeing said it informed all 737 operators last month about the software issue under which pilots may not have access to automated flight guidance during a specific landing scenario. “We shared information with operators that reinforced existing pilot procedures for safely handling such cases. Our engineers are working on a software update to permanently address the issue,” Boeing said in an emailed statement to Reuters. The Federal Aviation Administration said it was aware of a potential issue in a software update for the flight computers on certain Boeing 737 MAX airplanes and was working closely with Boeing and the airlines. “The FAA will convene a Corrective Action Review Board and will take immediate action if it identifies a safety concern,” the FAA said in a statement. Boeing has been under intense regulatory and safety scrutiny in recent years following two fatal 737 MAX crashes in 2018 and 2019 that led to a worldwide grounding of the aircraft, and after a mid-air cabin panel blowout on a nearly new Alaska Airlines MAX 9. Southwest Airlines and United Airlines have asked Boeing not to deliver new 737 MAX aircraft equipped with the affected software and instead requested an earlier version, according to WSJ. It was not immediately clear how many aircraft are operating with the flawed software, the report said. Boeing, airlines and regulators are assessing the issue and whether it poses a flight-safety concern, it added.

articles.title: German, Russian foreign ministers hold rare talks amid rising tensions
articles.summary: Russia’s Lavrov dismisses Wadephul’s call to abandon ‘dangerous path of escalation’ with Europe.
articles.body:
Germany’s Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has called on Russia to abandon its “dangerous path of escalation” with Germany, Europe and NATO during talks with his Russian counterpart, Sergey Lavrov, in New York.

The meeting on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly on Saturday — the first such talks since Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine — was requested by the German side, according to Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova. It was held before Lavrov’s address to world leaders.

In his speech on Saturday, Lavrov told the UNGA that Germany is not only Kyiv’s “main sponsor” but also seeks to be a leading military power in Europe.

“Does Berlin understand what this could lead to? Didn’t they … learn the lessons of World War II?” he asked.

Diplomatic relations between Berlin and Moscow have been frozen since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022.

They deteriorated further after a drone incident at Leipzig airport in eastern Germany last month, which Berlin blamed on Russia. Moscow has firmly denied involvement and accused Germany of fabricating evidence.

European countries have linked Russia to drone incursions near airports, military bases and critical infrastructure across the continent in the past year.

After his UN speech, Lavrov told a news conference that he had learned nothing new from his German counterpart in talks that Berlin had not already said publicly in its official statements.

“I told him that frankly … you could just have called me and said: ‘Read my statement,'” Lavrov said.

Still, the ministers discussed bilateral ties and the war in Ukraine, officials from both sides said.

Wadephul urged Lavrov to do “everything possible to reach an agreement on grain exports via the Black Sea”, a German delegation source said, as reported by the Reuters news agency.

The meeting comes amid diplomatic efforts to revive Russia and Ukraine’s Black Sea grain and energy exports that have been restricted by attacks on vessels and port infrastructure.

Lavrov told the news conference that Russia had been in talks with India, Egypt and Turkiye about proposals to ensure safe navigation in the Black Sea.

“There is a need for separate discussions with the Ukrainians, and not in the language of requests, but rather demands,” he said, blaming Ukraine for the attacks on vessels.

Kyiv has said it is open to agreements and blames all the fallout from the war on Russia and its invasion.

Wadephul notified his European allies of the meeting afterwards in a message seen by Reuters.

“I used this opportunity to reiterate our position on Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine and to call for an immediate and complete ceasefire, most pressingly with a focus on grain exports, and the energy infrastructure,” he wrote.

articles.title: The Trump administration said it would prioritize ending mother-to-child HIV transmission. Health workers say it cut services
articles.summary: Dr. Theopista Masenge was at the hospital in Mbeya, Tanzania, rolling out new treatments for children with high HIV viral loads when she got the call: Stop work, now.
articles.body: Dr. Theopista Masenge was at the hospital in Mbeya, Tanzania, rolling out new treatments for children with high HIV viral loads when she got the call: Stop work, now. It was January 2025, and the health care program the pediatrician was implementing, which provided services for HIV-exposed infants, children and pregnant women, had just received a letter from the now-dismantled United States Agency for International Development (USAID) directing it to halt all operations. “It was really, very abrupt, and I recall even the hospital managers were running up and down like, ‘What are we going to do?’” said Masenge, who lost her job not long after. Almost overnight, “the system that was built for almost 40 years was gone.” “Everything has been disrupted,” she told CNN. More than a year later, she said that disruptions to HIV/AIDS services for children and pregnant women remain across Tanzania, even though limited US government funding has returned. It’s a pattern playing out across Africa, Asia and beyond as the Trump administration’s cuts to global health funding and dismantling of USAID have severely disrupted the United States’ flagship HIV/AIDS program, PEPFAR, according to a new study by the Foundation for AIDS Research (amfAR). The study, conducted with Johns Hopkins University and published in July, surveyed 166 organizations that received PEPFAR funding last year across 46 countries (representing 23% of all PEPFAR partner organizations). Although the US government said last September that HIV services to prevent mother-to-child transmission would be prioritized and protected from funding cuts, the amfAR survey found that 63% of respondents reported disruptions to those services. That includes 22% of surveyed organizations that said they ended those mother-to-child prevention services entirely amid the funding cuts. “Even if the administration’s intention was to not touch these programs, PEPFAR (funding) awards generally aren’t sort of specific to doing one individual task,” said Elise Lankiewicz, a senior policy associate at amfAR. “There was really no way to protect very singular parts of the system while dismantling others.” It comes as 1,714 health clinics once supported by PEPFAR closed last year around the world, according to the organizations surveyed. “I’m not so worried in terms of supplies and medications, but I’m super worried about the quality of care for the children, for the mothers,” said Masenge, now the president of the Paediatric Association of Tanzania, regarding the situation in her area. “People are not going back to the facility to pick up their medication because they feel like the services have really become worse, and the early infant diagnosis is suffering similarly.” PEPFAR, which was established by the George W. Bush administration in 2003, is credited with saving more than 26 million lives and preventing millions of infections, mostly in Africa, according to the World Health Organization and the program’s own data. It’s one of the US government’s hallmark global health programs that is now experiencing significant funding cuts, as the administration transitions to a strategy of striking new agreements with aid-recipient nations and demanding more co-financing from them. A US State Department spokesperson told CNN that the amfAR survey has “flawed” methodology and said that “the Trump Administration has strengthened PEPFAR through clear strategic direction, promoting greater recipient-country ownership, and sharpening the program’s focus on measurable health outcomes. As a result, the number of children testing positive and on treatment for HIV has continued to decline.” While it’s true that the number of children starting new HIV treatment fell last year, experts say that’s not necessarily a marker of success. Declines in the number of children being tested and monitored for HIV indicate that children are losing access to care and falling through the cracks, according to the Elizabeth Glaser Pediatric Aids Foundation. Meanwhile, disruptions to data gathering and reporting have made it more difficult to spot negative outcomes. The State Department spokesperson added: “Today, we are focusing on real outcomes: fewer new infections, mature programs transitioning to local management, and countries advancing toward long-term self-reliance … FY2025 Q4 data show that as of September 30, 2025, the U.S. government supported lifesaving HIV treatment for 20.6 million people living with HIV in more than 50 countries.” ‘HIV crisis hiding in plain sight’ The Elizabeth Glaser Pediatric Aids Foundation has called the drops in pediatric diagnosis and treatment an “HIV crisis hiding in plain sight.” “Every single indicator in the pediatric HIV cascade shows decline,” the foundation said. Its president, Dr. Doris Macharia, added: “Where the (PEPFAR) program reaches children, it works. But the data tell us that far fewer are now being reached.” Despite US government carve-outs for “life-saving” work to continue in relation to pregnant and breastfeeding women, amfAR’s analysis of the latest US government data found that HIV testing for pregnant women declined slightly, by 2%, at the end of 2025 compared with the same time period a year before. Testing for babies declined further, by at least 6%, although some health facilities reported far worse metrics for infant testing. Meanwhile, respondents to the amfAR survey reported that the Orphans and Vulnerable Children Program, aimed at helping high-risk children access HIV care and other general health services, has also been severely disrupted. KFF, a nonprofit health policy research organization, found that the number of children and family members served by that program fell by about 4.8 million in 2025 compared with the year before. Another recent analysis by the Clinton Health Access Initiative found that the number of children getting on medications used to treat HIV declined 15% in 2025 compared with the year before across eight countries that it studied. The organization said that reflects the negative impacts of HIV test kit shortages, as well as “ongoing integration of pediatric HIV services into general health facilities without adequate provider training and support.” Beyond medications and basic care, PEPFAR once provided many “wraparound services” designed to prevent infections, encourage marginalized people to come to clinics and keep people from falling off their treatment plans, according to HIV/AIDS experts who spoke to CNN. “I would expect those are the first things that are going to drop off, especially in countries with limited funds to replace what’s been lost from PEPFAR,” amfAR’s Lankiewicz said. When it comes to preventing mother-to-child transmission, those wraparound services include things like paying community health care workers to follow up with mothers about scheduling appointments or providing community education about how HIV can be transmitted to babies. What is preserved will depend on the ability of each country’s government to upkeep and pay for services, experts said. “On top of that, then we have this issue with money not flowing. So even though PEPFAR received the regular amount of appropriations from Congress in the last year, that money is not actually moving,” Lankiewicz added. CNN has previously reported on the Trump administration underspending roughly $1.7 billion that Congress has already approved for the flagship HIV/AIDS program, as well as redirecting $2 billion in funding intended for global health programs to cover the cost of closing USAID. Hard to see full picture of disruptions Changes to the implementation of PEPFAR and spending cuts have affected not only health services but also data collection. PEPFAR’s robust data collection was once a valuable resource for researchers and health care providers around the world. But the Trump administration has stopped releasing the program’s quarterly reports and withheld some of the data. The State Department said earlier this year that the US government had “greater confidence in data” from the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025 but added that “earlier quarters experienced reporting and implementation challenges which limit data interpretability.” Experts warn that the data upheaval makes it harder to see the full picture of health service disruptions and final outcomes. “You don’t always see the impact on outcomes till it’s too late,” said Jennifer Kates, director of global and public health policy at KFF. “And that would be a crisis, if we get to a point in a year or so where we look back and say more babies died and more children were born with HIV.” For example, the US government has suggested that declines in the number of children being treated for HIV indicate that programs to prevent infections in the first place are working. But the Elizabeth Glaser Pediatric AIDS Foundation has said that “does not explain such a dramatic and sudden drop of 54,000 children already on treatment.” When it comes to the decline in the number of infants being tested for HIV, Kates said, it could lead to researchers and program-implementers being in the dark. She asked, “If there’s not as much detection going on, are we going to even know what is happening for babies?”

articles.title: Germany’s AfD is so extreme it’s putting off other far-right parties
articles.summary: The rise of Germany’s Alternative for Germany (AfD) is causing widespread alarm, including in unexpected quarters - other far-right European parties.
articles.body: The rise of Germany’s Alternative for Germany (AfD) is causing widespread alarm, including in unexpected quarters - other far-right European parties. While the German party is winning record levels of support at home, some of its closest ideological allies elsewhere in Europe are keeping it at arm’s length. That tension was again on display after Germany’s recent state elections. In the state of Saxony-Anhalt earlier this month, the AfD made historic gains when it won 43.8% of the vote, falling just three seats short of an outright majority. Elections in Mecklenburg- Vorpommern and Berlin last weekend also showed a exodus from mainstream parties to the fringes, notably the AfD. Several of the bloc’s far-right party leaders have offered their congratulations, including Geert Wilder of the Netherlands’ Party for Freedom, Viktor Orbàn of Hungary’s Fidesz and Santiago Abascal of Spain’s Vox, who hailed the AfD’s advance as “a “great hope for Germany and Europe.” But some of Europe’s biggest far-right parties - including in France, Italy and Britain - have been silent. France’s National Rally (RN), once one of the AfD’s closest partners, said even before the Saxony-Anhalt vote that renewed cooperation with the AfD was “not planned.” For party leader Marine Le Pen, there is a domestic calculation in play as well as an ideological one. Under her leadership, the National Rally has embraced what it calls “detoxification”, shifting the party away from the overt xenophobia of its roots under her father, Jean-Marie Le Pen, toward the political mainstream. Softer rhetoric She has also worked to move the party’s brand away from the stain of two of its founders’ Nazi past. Its anti-immigration rhetoric is softer, its doors open to mixed-race citizens that her father’s generation might not have welcomed as the “right kind” of French. Since Hamas’ October 7 attacks against Israel, she’s made condemning antisemitism a powerful arm in her rebranding. The RN, in its previous guise as the National Front, had long been a collaborator with the AfD in the European Parliament. But comments from a senior AfD figure talking down the criminal role of Hitler’s SS paramilitary group in World War II as well as the emergence of a secret plan by the German party to expel people of foreign origin en masse crossed the RN’s red lines. An alliance with the AfD wasn’t compatible with the RN’s new image. In May 2024, the French party broke ranks and ties with the German far right. The split was evident following the AfD’s recent successes, with the RN’s top leadership notably silent. With the 2027 presidential election on the horizon – Marine Le Pen’s best chance yet to win the Elysée Palace – that’s likely a strategy to avoid any negative blowback. “We have real problems on both style and substance. We do not consider them to be our allies in Germany,” RN lawmaker Franck Allisio told television channel LCI on September 6, the day of the Saxony-Anhalt vote. ‘Extremist’ label In comparison to the RN, the AfD has made no effort to purge itself of its extremist factions despite now also appealing to a wide range of voters, said Grégoire Roos, director of the Europe, Russia and Eurasia programs at the Chatham House think tank. The AfD has rejected accusations of right-wing extremism, with the party’s co-leaders previously describing Germany’s domestic intelligence agency’s classification of it as “extremist” as an attempt to “distort democratic competition.” “Unlike the National Rally that has worked extremely hard to wipe out any morally disturbing elements… the AfD hasn’t conducted such a clean-up,” Roos told CNN. Figures within the AfD are also comfortable talking about the Nazi era as though not everything from that period of history should be “thrown in the garbage,” another aspect which makes the party unpalatable to most of its European peers, Roos said. The more radical far-right French party of Éric Zemmour, Reconquest, however, welcomed the AfD’s win in Saxony-Anhalt. Leading Reconquest MEP Sarah Knafo called the results “historic” in an election night X post. “The European peoples have shown a great deal of patience. Today, they want to take their destiny back into their own hands. An entire continent is rising up,” she said. In this vein, the AfD is not completely alone. It helped create the Europe of Sovereign Nations group in the European Parliament after its expulsion from Identity and Democracy. The smaller, more isolated group includes nationalist parties such as Reconquest, as well as Bulgaria’s Revival, Hungary’s Our Homeland Movement, Poland’s New Hope and Slovakia’s Republic Movement. Meloni keeps her distance The far-right Brothers of Italy has also not embraced the AfD, with party leader Giorgia Meloni, the Italian prime minister, instead pursuing a strategy of building influence within Europe’s political mainstream. Her party sits in the European Conservatives and Reformists group, which is more integrated into the European Parliament’s institutional mainstream than the AfD’s Europe of Sovereign Nations grouping. The two parties have deep foreign policy disagreements, with Meloni’s party supporting NATO and Ukraine, while the AfD advocates against sending weapons to Ukraine and wants to lift sanctions on Russia. Meloni has called these differences “irreconcilable.” Nigel Farage, who spearheads Britain’s hard-right Reform UK party, has described the AfD as a “mixed bag.” Asked on a podcast with Axel Springer CEO Mathias Döpfner in April what his party’s main differences with the AfD are, Farage said, “I think the pro-Putin stuff, I find it hard to understand.” The AfD’s ties to some dictators were “very, very difficult,” he added. The AfD’s foreign policy positions have made it an awkward partner for many. The party contains competing currents over Germany’s relationship with Russia and the US, while its support for closer relations with Moscow separates it from other European right-wing parties. It has also adopted a strong anti-aid rhetoric regarding Ukraine, setting it apart from some, although not all, of Europe’s populist parties. The party is “very much radical when it comes to Ukraine and Russia,” Roos believes. “Listening to the AfD, you would almost feel like Russia has not invaded Ukraine, that Russia is not committing crimes every single day in Ukraine or killing civilians.” Russia has repeatedly denied accusations of targeting civilians in Ukraine. Foreign influence Additionally, parties such as France’s RN have made efforts to disassociate themselves from foreign powers such as Russia and China, while the AfD has not. Last year, the AfD’s links to Beijing were thrust into the spotlight when a former top party aide was convicted in Germany of spying for China. The AfD has also courted support in Washington. President Donald Trump took to social media to congratulate the party on its landslide victory in Saxony-Anhalt, ending his message with a German variant of his Make America Great Again acronym, “MGGA!” Elon Musk, who has championed the AfD for years, also expressed his delight. The AfD has maintained a “strong association with Trump and the MAGA movement, which in France, like many European countries, has become increasingly unpopular,” Roos said. Hypothetically, if the AfD were to make significant regional gains in Germany, it would likely push for a strong nationalist agenda as well as for strengthening relations with Moscow and the lifting of Russian oil and gas sanctions at the European level, Roos said. He pointed out, though, that German foreign policy is vested in the Chancellor’s office, which may limit sudden shifts even if regional support for the AfD’s positions grows. He added that German democracy remains solid due to its independent judiciary and constitutional court, designed to keep political power in check. The AfD’s growing strength presents Europe’s far right with a dilemma. If the party continues to gain popularity in Germany, ignoring it could become more complicated. But embracing it could carry political costs for far-right parties that want to demonstrate that they can move from the political margins into government.

articles.body: Fans of the beloved video game have been glued to the edge of their seats over news of the third season of the live-action series, ‘The Last of Us.' The release is slated for sometime in 2027, while new cast members are slowly being added for the new storyline. According to recent reports, voice actors who starred in the ‘The Last of Us’ video game and lent their voices to some of the well-known characters are joining the official cast of the live-action series.‘The Last of Us’ game voiceover artist joins season three of the live-action showEntertainment Weekly reported that actress Laura Bailey, who lent her voice to Abby in ‘The Last of Us’ game, has officially joined the live-action series’ upcoming season. She brought the character to life and even worked on motion capture to help structure the character. Other than her, according to reports shared online, star Ian Alexander is also joining the live-action show. He voiced and performed motion capture for the character Lev in the video game ‘The Last of Us Part II.’While Bailey played Abby’s role in the game, she will be playing a character called Elizabeth in the upcoming season. As for her opinions on passing the torch to Dever for Abby’s character, Bailey added, “She’s just phenomenal; every moment that I saw that she was in, I just loved how much she brought to the character and made it her own. It’s kind of like watching your child get up and start walking for the first time. Once you put it out there, it’s somebody else's, and she’s just embraced it.”Some of the other new cast members include Peter Sarsgaard, Clea Duvall, and Jason Ritter. While not much is known about the coming season of the post-apocalyptic show, it is said to be centered mainly around Abby’s point of view.

articles.title: Florida man, 76, with suspended license allegedly admits to driving under the influence of rum, cocaine
articles.summary: Charles Ducking, 76, allegedly showed deputies his rum cup and admitted to doing cocaine minutes before a traffic stop in Polk County, Florida.
articles.body: A 76-year-old Florida man with a suspended license allegedly admitted during a traffic stop that he had been drinking rum — later telling deputies he had also recently used cocaine — just four months after a separate DUI arrest, authorities said. Charles Ducking, 76, of Lake Wales, was pulled over after a sheriff's deputy allegedly observed him swerving while driving along U.S. Highway 27 in Waverly, according to the Polk County Sheriff's Office. The deputy detected the odor of alcohol and noticed that Ducking allegedly had slurred speech and watery eyes. When asked for his driver's license, Ducking allegedly told the deputy it had been suspended. FLORIDA MAN ARRESTED FOR DUI AFTER TROOPERS ALLEGEDLY FIND 34 OPEN ALCOHOL CONTAINERS IN VEHICLE "Well, I can't show you my driver's license cuz it's suspended cuz DUI. And I have been drinking a little bit right now," he said, according to the sheriff's office. Officials said Ducking then showed the deputy a silver thermal cup containing a brown liquid. "This here is my rum I'm drinking," he said, according to the sheriff's office. IOWA WOMAN WITH A PRIOR CONVICTION UNDER HER BELT ARRESTED FOR OWI ON LAWN MOWER A traffic deputy who responded to conduct a DUI investigation immediately recognized Ducking from a previous DUI arrest in May, the sheriff's office said. Officials said deputies also found a small orange container containing cocaine during a search of Ducking's vehicle, which allegedly prompted Ducking to tell law enforcement he had "done a line" 10 minutes before he was pulled over. During field sobriety tests, Ducking displayed several indicators of impairment, and breath tests registered blood alcohol concentration readings of .094 and .095, above Florida's .08 legal limit for drivers. "While we appreciate Charles Ducking's cooperation during the traffic stop, the fact of the matter is, he is lucky he hasn't yet killed someone or himself while driving drunk and high on drugs," Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd said in a statement. "He has tempted fate too many times, and he needs to make some serious changes in his life before it's too late," Judd continued. "I am proud of my deputies for their proactive patrolling to find impaired drivers and get them off the road." TIGER WOODS STRIKES PLEA DEAL IN FLORIDA ROLLOVER CRASH CASE, LOSES DRIVER'S LICENSE FOR 5 YEARS Ducking was arrested and booked into the Polk County Jail. He was charged with DUI — fourth or subsequent offense — possession of cocaine, driving with a suspended license and possession of drug paraphernalia. According to the sheriff's office, Ducking was previously arrested for DUI in May. He was released from jail days later after posting bond on the condition that he not possess or consume alcohol. articles.title: Ethiopia’s army promises restraint amid fears of new civil war
articles.summary: Army chief accuses Eritrea of funding and supporting armed groups to weaken Ethiopia.
articles.body:
Ethiopia’s federal military has said it is handling rising tensions in the country’s north with restraint, as fears grow that Ethiopia could be heading towards another civil war.

In his first comments on the recent military developments, Army Chief of Staff Field Marshal Berhanu Jula said the army was responding to what he called provocations from the Tigray front with “wisdom and restraint”.

He accused Eritrea of funding and supporting armed groups to weaken Ethiopia, describing the “Tsimdo” alliance as an extension of a longstanding pattern of hostile alliances, which he said cannot confront the state without outside backing.

Eritrea, wary that landlocked Ethiopia may be seeking to invade it to gain access to the Red Sea, denied the accusations.

The fighting has spread from Tigray into neighbouring Afar and Amhara regions after seven armed groups announced an alliance , the Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival, committed to removing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government.

In Afar, the latest battles have taken place around Abala, where the military has been trying to prevent rebels from seizing control.

Separately, in North Wollo, a zone of Amhara bordering Tigray, the army said on Thursday it had killed 272 Tigrayan fighters and wounded 260 in a counter-offensive, reporting heavy losses for the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF).

The TPLF’s Tigray Army said the federal government had launched a “full-scale offensive” involving infantry, mechanised units and drones.

Abdisalam Balema, a TPLF central committee member, told Al Jazeera the situation had become a “full war”.

Fighting has also continued around Sama, Soqota and Raya Alamata, with government forces reportedly closing in on the town of Alamata.

The army command said it prefers a strategy of “strategic calm” over a large-scale military confrontation , arguing the Tigray front’s popular support is dwindling and its leadership divided.

Internet access was reportedly cut across northern Ethiopia on Friday, a day after the UN said it was alarmed by reports of drones being used against civilians there.

The renewed fighting has put the 2022 Pretoria Agreement, which ended a brutal two-year civil war in Tigray, under severe strain. It comes weeks after Washington lifted sanctions on Ethiopia and Eritrea tied to atrocities from the last war, saying the “national emergency … has expired”.

It marks the most serious challenge yet to that agreement, raising fears of a wider regional conflict that could draw in armed groups from across Ethiopia.

Addressing the UN General Assembly, Ethiopia’s president sought to portray the country as a force for regional stability, accusing unnamed external actors of meddling in Ethiopia’s affairs while highlighting Addis Ababa’s role in supporting peace efforts in neighbouring Sudan.

Alemayehu Weldemariam, a professor of law at Indiana University, told Al Jazeera that the federal government bears much of the blame for the collapse of the Pretoria Agreement.

“This war has been in the making for a while now. Much of the provisions in the cessation of hostilities [in the 2022 agreement] were primarily sabotaged by the federal government itself,” he said, citing fuel, service and cash restrictions imposed on Tigray, and the government’s failure to set up the interim administration the deal had promised.

“What was supposed to be an interim arrangement turned out to be permanent,” with Tigray excluded from national elections since, he added.

articles.title: Two giant pandas on their way to Zoo Atlanta from China after Trump-Xi-Trump summit
articles.summary: Two giant pandas departed Chengdu in southwestern China early Sunday for their new homes in Atlanta as part of an agreement between the Chinese and American governments.
articles.body: BANGKOK — Two giant pandas departed Chengdu in southwestern China early Sunday for their new homes in Atlanta as part of an agreement between the Chinese and American governments. While in Washington for a three-day summit with U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping announced that the pandas would arrive in Atlanta in the coming days. The loan of the pandas to the Atlanta zoo was one of the few concrete outcomes to come out of the state visit, which saw expressions of goodwill between the leaders, but no fixes to any of the long-standing differences between the two countries. Atlanta said farewell to its last pandas in 2024, leaving the zoo without the bears. The new agreement was announced back in April, but without any dates. Ping Ping and Fu Shuang are the two adult pandas that will be on loan to Zoo Atlanta for 10 years as part of the agreement. Both pandas were born in 2020 and were kept at the Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding. Ping Ping, the male, has dark black circles around his eyes, while Fu Shuang, the female, has a forehead that protrudes a bit, according to the Xinhua News Agency. China has long used the pandas as part of its diplomacy globally, deploying the bears in loan programs as expressions of goodwill and letting loan agreements lapse when tensions arise. Xi had said the loan program was an example of “friendship between the Chinese and Americans.”

articles.title: Suffolk and Essex NHS remove 10 staff over Noah Woods data breach
articles.summary: East Suffolk and North Essex NHS Foundation Trust says it has launched an "urgent" investigation.
articles.body:
Ten NHS staff have been removed from duty or suspended after a data breach involving the medical records of three-year-old Noah Woods.

Launching an "urgent" investigation, Dr Martin Mansfield, deputy chief medical officer at East Suffolk and North Essex NHS Foundation Trust, said that any unauthorised access of patient data was "completely unacceptable".

The trust has apologised to Noah's family and said disciplinary action would be taken if needed.

A major search for Noah was carried out in the village of Brantham, Suffolk, after the child went missing on 15 September. His body was found the next day in nearby water by police divers.

A spokesperson for the trust said 10 employees had been "removed from active duty or suspended whilst investigations are concluded".

In the statement issued on Sunday, Mansfield said of the data breach: "Immediate steps were also taken to secure the records and prevent further access that was not for a legitimate, clinical reason.

"We have reported the matter to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO), and we will continue to keep Noah's family informed as our investigation progresses."

At least 1,300 people helped in the search for Noah in the 24 hours before he was found.

A tribute issued by his family called him a "happy, cheeky, playful" boy who loved to laugh. His mother urged other parents to "hold their children a little tighter and cherish every moment".

An inquest, which opened on Friday, heard that the three-year-old had left a play area "through a gap in the fence".

Assistant coroner Jyoti Gill said it was a "very sad and tragic death" as she opened and adjourned the inquest in Ipswich.
